makaleler.baslik: Transverse versus longitudinal mucosotomy during peroral endoscopic myotomy: results of a multicenter randomized controlled trial.
makaleler.baslik_tr: POEM İşleminde Transvers ve Longitudinal Mukozotomi Karşılaştırması
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 140 hastalık çok merkezli RCT'de, transvers mukozotomi submukozal tünele girişi hızlandırdı (228 sn'ye karşı 269 sn), hemostaz ihtiyacını azalttı (RR 0,68) ve pnömoperitoneum riskini düşürdü (RR 0,67). Yöntem, POEM prosedüründe verimliliği artırmaktadır.
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Peroral endoscopic myotomy (POEM) is an established first-line therapy for achalasia; however, technical variability persists in key procedural steps. The optimal orientation of mucosal entry remains uncertain. We evaluated whether transverse mucosotomy improves procedural efficiency and reduces gas-related events compared with the conventional longitudinal approach.
METHODS: In this multicenter, parallel-group randomized clinical trial conducted at three tertiary centers, 140 adults undergoing POEM were assigned (1:1) to a standardized 15-mm transverse or longitudinal mucosotomy. The primary outcome was time from initial mucosal incision to effective entry into the submucosal tunnel, assessed by independent anonymized video review using predefined objective timestamp criteria. Secondary outcomes included need for hemostasis, mucosotomy closure time, number of clips used, gas-related events, and 30-day complications. Analyses followed the intention-to-treat principle.
RESULTS: All randomized patients were included in the primary analysis. Transverse mucosotomy significantly reduced time to submucosal entry (median 228 vs. 269 s; adjusted mean difference - 44 s; 95% CI - 78 to - 10), need for hemostasis (38.6% vs. 57.1%; relative risk 0.68; 95% CI 0.49-0.95), closure time (662 vs. 1020 s; p < 0.001), and number of clips used (median 3 vs. 7; rate ratio 0.44; 95% CI 0.36-0.54). Pneumoperitoneum occurred less frequently with the transverse approach (34.3% vs. 51.4%; relative risk 0.67; 95% CI 0.46-0.97). Rates of serious adverse events and 30-day readmission were low and comparable between groups.
CONCLUSIONS: In a multicenter randomized trial, transverse mucosotomy during POEM improved intraoperative efficiency and reduced gas-related events without compromising short-term safety. These findings support mucosal entry orientation as a modifiable technical factor that may optimize procedural workflow and resource utilization in submucosal endoscopic surgery.
CLINICAL TRIALS REGISTRY: NCT07425977.

makaleler.baslik: Cryoballoon Ablation for Eradication of Sporadic and Familial Non-Ampullary Proximal Duodenal Adenomas (with video).
makaleler.baslik_tr: Duodenal Adenomların Tedavisinde Kriyobalon Ablasyonun Güvenliği ve Etkinliği
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 31 hastada 43 duodenal adenomun değerlendirildiği prospektif çok merkezli çalışmada, kriyobalon ablasyon ile %87 başarı oranı elde edildi. İşlem sonrası ciddi komplikasyon izlenmedi ve %6,1 oranında hafif ağrı raporlandı. Yöntem, duodenal adenomlar için güvenli ve etkili bir endoskopik alternatif olabilir.
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Endoscopic resection of all sporadic duodenal adenomas (DAs) is recommended due to risk for progression.
AIM: We assessed the safety and efficacy of Cryoballoon ablation for complete endoscopic and histologic eradication (CE).
METHODS: In a prospective multicenter nonrandomized trial conducted in academic medical centers, we enrolled patients with benign familial and sporadic non-ampullary DAs in the first or second portion with size 1-5 cm, thickness <4 mm (Paris 2a,2b,1s) involving <50% circumference and <3 duodenal folds, with no prior ablation or surgery. We treated at baseline and every 3 months until CE was achieved within 12 months or at last follow-up.
PRIMARY ENDPOINTS: safety and CE of treated DAs by patient and by polyp using intention-to-treat analysis. Secondary endpoints: technical success, ablation time, number of CBA sessions, progression rate.
RESULTS: We treated 31 patients (5 FAP, 26 non-FAP) (23% prior EMR) with 43 DAs, in a median of 2 procedures within 6.7 minutes or 2.6 min/DA. Technical success was 97%. We noted CE of all treated DAs in 27/31 (87%) of patients and 34/43 (79%) polyps, with no difference between sporadic (88%) or FAP (80%). In 3/5 FAP patients, CBA downgraded their Spigelman class (Stage 3 to 2, Stage 2 to 0). DA size was the only independent predictor of CE, all DAs <2cm were eradicated. There were no treatment-related serious adverse events, including bleeding or perforation. Post-CBA pain was mild (incidence 6.1%), none required narcotics.
CONCLUSION: CBA may be a safe, effective, and efficient alternative endoscopic therapy for selected non-ampullary DAs in the proximal duodenum. (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03847636).

makaleler.baslik: Increased Adoption of Robot-Assisted Appendectomy Without Improved Outcomes and Lower Modeled Value.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Robotik apendektominin klinik sonuçları ve maliyet analizi
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 2.257 robotik ve 4.514 laparoskopik apendektominin karşılaştırıldığı çalışmada, komplikasyon oranları benzer bulunmuştur (OR 1,06; p=0,61). Robotik cerrahi 15,48 dakika daha uzun sürmüş ve maliyeti anlamlı derecede yüksek bulunmuştur.
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Robot-assisted appendectomy use is increasing despite uncertain clinical benefit and economic value relative to laparoscopy. We evaluated comparative outcomes, operative efficiency, and modeled value.
STUDY DESIGN: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults undergoing intended minimally invasive appendectomy for appendicitis using 2022-2024 ACS NSQIP data. Robotic utilization was assessed among 140,148 patients. Clinical outcomes were compared using 1:2 propensity-score matching. The primary endpoint combined unplanned conversion to open surgery, postoperative transfusion, organ-space surgical-site infection, and reoperation. Surgical costs were simulated using literature-derived inputs; value incorporated risk-adjusted outcomes and simulated costs.
RESULTS: Robotic utilization increased from 0.7% in 2022 to 2.7% in 2024. Among 2,257 robot-assisted and 4,514 matched laparoscopic cases, the primary composite occurred in 5.5% versus 5.3% (OR 1.06; 95% CI 0.85-1.32; P=.61). Robot-assisted appendectomy required 15.48 additional operative minutes (95% CI 13.66-17.31; P<.001), without significant differences in readmission, mortality, or length of stay. Median simulated costs were $4,526 versus $2,416. Laparoscopic-to-robotic modeled value ratios ranged from 1.53 to 1.80. Even assuming no incremental robotic procedural-cost premium, laparoscopy retained higher modeled value for the primary composite (ratio 1.31; 95% CI 1.09-1.54). Exploratory analyses of complicated appendicitis and BMI ≥40 kg/m² identified no significant clinical advantage with robotics.
CONCLUSIONS: Robot-assisted appendectomy utilization increased nearly fourfold without an observed improvement in short-term outcomes. Longer operative time, higher simulated costs, and lower modeled value persisted across sensitivity analyses, supporting continued scrutiny of robotic adoption for an operation effectively performed laparoscopically.

makaleler.baslik: Pre-puncture EUS-based prediction of technical failure during EUS-guided hepaticogastrostomy: development and internal validation of a three-factor model.
makaleler.baslik_tr: EUS-Guttlu Hepatikogastrostomi Teknik Başarısızlık Tahmini
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 453 EUS-HGS girişiminin incelendiği retrospektif çalışmada ilk denemede teknik başarısızlık oranı %11,7 bulundu. Küçük safra kanalı çapı, akut iğne-kanal açısı ve uzun karaciğer parankim uzunluğu teknik başarısızlıkla ilişkili bulundu (AUC 0,932). Model, delme öncesi risk tahmini için ön çerçeve sunmaktadır.
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Technical failure during EUS-guided hepaticogastrostomy (EUS-HGS) remains clinically relevant, yet most previously reported predictors are assessed only after bile duct puncture or guidewire manipulation has already been attempted. We aimed to identify EUS-assessable anatomical factors measurable before bile duct puncture and to develop an internally validated model for predicting first-attempt technical failure during EUS-HGS.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed consecutive patients who underwent attempted EUS-HGS between January 2015 and December 2025 at a single tertiary center. The primary outcome was first-attempt technical failure of EUS-HGS. Pre-puncture EUS images were reviewed to measure bile duct diameter at the intended puncture site, needle-duct angle, and hepatic parenchymal length. Independent predictors were identified using multivariable logistic regression, and a three-factor prediction model was developed. Discrimination, calibration, and internal validation with 2,000 bootstrap resamples were assessed.
RESULTS: Among 453 attempted EUS-HGS procedures, first-attempt technical success was achieved in 400 (88.3%) and first-attempt technical failure occurred in 53 (11.7%). Smaller bile duct diameter (OR 0.282 per 1-mm increase; 95% CI 0.181-0.440), a more acute needle-duct angle (OR 0.632 per 10° increase; 95% CI 0.533-0.748), and longer hepatic parenchymal length (OR 1.144 per 1-mm increase; 95% CI 1.080-1.212) were independently associated with first-attempt technical failure. The combined three-factor model showed excellent apparent discrimination (AUC 0.932; 95% CI 0.897-0.961), with an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.927 after bootstrap validation. The optimal cutoff probability was 0.130, yielding 86.8% sensitivity and 85.5% specificity. Observed failure rates were 1.7% in the low-risk group, 9.0% in the intermediate-risk group, and 51.9% in the high-risk group.
CONCLUSIONS: A three-factor model based on anatomical variables assessable on EUS before bile duct puncture showed excellent apparent discrimination and good calibration for predicting first-attempt technical failure during EUS-HGS. This internally validated model provides a preliminary framework for pre-puncture risk estimation; however, its clinical application remains hypothesis-generating and requires prospective multicenter external validation before implementation in clinical decision-making.

makaleler.baslik: Robotic pancreatic enucleation versus laparoscopic pancreatic enucleation: a meta-analysis.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Robotik ve Laparoskopik Pankreas Enükleasyonu Meta-analizi
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 272 hastayı kapsayan 5 çalışmanın meta-analizinde, robotik ve laparoskopik pankreas enükleasyonu arasında operasyon süresi, kan kaybı ve fistül gelişimi açısından anlamlı fark bulunmadı. Robotik grupta hastanede kalış süresi daha kısa olsa da klinik üstünlük için kanıtlar yetersizdir.
makaleler.ozet: Pancreatic enucleation (PE) is an operation that spares pancreatic parenchyma and thereby preserves glandular function, and it is now widely favoured for benign and low-grade malignant pancreatic neoplasms. Whether adding robotic assistance brings benefit beyond the standard laparoscopic route, however, remains an open question. This meta-analysis therefore contrasted robotic pancreatic enucleation (RPE) with laparoscopic pancreatic enucleation (LPE) with respect to perioperative efficacy and safety. Records of cohort studies that contrasted RPE with LPE were retrieved from the Cochrane Library, PubMed, the Wanfang, Embase and China National Knowledge Infrastructure, covering each database from inception to 1 September 2026. Two investigators working in duplicate screened the records, extracted the data and rated methodological quality with the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS). R 4.5.3 with the meta package was used for pooling; mean differences (MDs) and risk ratios (RRs) were presented with their 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Publication-bias and sensitivity analyses were omitted because fewer than 10 eligible studies were available. Five studies met the eligibility criteria (each scoring NOS ≥ 7) and together enrolled 272 patients, 144 in the LPE arm and 128 in the RPE arm. Operation time (MD 0.20, 95% CI - 38.98 to 39.39, P = 0.99), intraoperative blood loss (MD 14.60, 95% CI - 3.39 to 32.58, P = 0.11), postoperative pancreatic fistula (risk ratio [RR] 1.21, 95% CI 0.89-1.64, P = 0.23), postoperative bleeding (RR 0.43, 95% CI 0.06-2.97, P = 0.39), and major complications (RR 1.28, 95% CI 0.54-3.00, P = 0.58) did not differ significantly between groups. Postoperative hospital stay was statistically shorter in the RPE group (MD 1.22, 95% CI 0.29-2.16, P = 0.01); however, this finding should be interpreted cautiously and does not, by itself, establish a clinically meaningful recovery advantage. The available evidence is insufficient to demonstrate a clear overall difference between robotic and laparoscopic pancreatic enucleation in perioperative efficacy or safety. Although postoperative hospital stay was shorter in the RPE group in the pooled analysis, the small observational evidence base and potential residual confounding preclude a firm conclusion that robotic surgery provides a recovery advantage. Larger, well-designed prospective multicentre studies are needed.

tez.baslik: Laparoskopik kolesistektomi yapılan hastalarda piyes bütünlüğünün önemi ve piyes bütünlüğüne etki eden faktörler
tez.baslik_tr: Laparoskopik kolesistektomide piyes bütünlüğünü etkileyen faktörler
tez.kisa_ozet: 1407 hastanın retrospektif incelendiği çalışmada, piyes bütünlüğünün cinsiyet, endo-bag kullanımı, safra kesesi duvar kalınlığı ve cerrah ile ilişkili olduğu, ancak taş boyutu veya inflamatuar belirteçlerle ilişkili olmadığı saptanmıştır.
tez.ozet: Amaç: Laparoskopik kolesistektomi semptomatik safra kesesi hastalıklarının tedavisinde minimal invaziv bir cerrahi prosedürdür ve güvenli bir yöntem olarak kullanımı yaygındır. Laparoskopik kolesistektomide çıkarılan piyes hem cerrah hem de patolog açısından klinik öneme sahiptir. Bununla birlikte, literatürde laparoskopik kolesistektomide piyes bütünlüğünü etkileyen faktörler yeterince incelenmemiştir. Bu çalışmada, piyes bütünlüğünün hangi faktörlerden etkilendiğini ortaya koymak amaçlanmıştır. Yöntem: Çalışmada, 2019 ila 2025 yılları arasında Kahramanmaraş Sütçü İmam Üniversitesi Tıp Fakültesi Hastanesi Genel Cerrahi Ana Bilim Dalı'nda 1407 hastaya uygulanan laparoskopik kolesistektomilerin patoloji sonuçları retrospektif olarak incelenmiştir. Piyesin bütün halinde olması, açılmış olması veya bütünlüğünün bozulmuş olması durumlarının hastaların yaşı, cinsiyeti, endo-bag kullanımı, taş tespit edilme durumu, taş boyutu, safra kesesi duvar kalınlığı, cerrah, White Blood Cell (WBC), C-reaktif protein (CRP),Direkt Bilirubin (D.Bilirubin) ve Karaciğer fonksiyon testleri (KCFT) değerleri tarafından belirlenip belirlenmedikleri araştırılmıştır. KCFT değeri olarak Aspartat Aminotransferaz (AST), Alanin aminotransferaz (ALT), Gama-Glutamil Transferaz (GGT), Alkalen fosfataz (ALP) değerleri bir grup halinde incelendi.En az bir değerin yüksekliğinde KCFT değeri yüksek olarak değerlendirildi. Bulgular: Hastaların %31,1'i erkek, %68,9'u kadındır. Hastaların yaşları 18 ila 90 arasında değişmektedir ve yaş ortalaması 49,5±14,93'tür. Hastaların %48,3'ünde piyes bir bütün halinde iken %40,0'ında açılmış halde ve %11,7'sinde ise bütünlüğü bozulmuş haldedir. Endo-bag kullanım oranı %40,2'dir. Taş tespit edilme oranı %84,4'tür. Safra kesesi duvar kalınlığı 0,1 cm ila 3,50 cm arasında değişmektedir ve ortalama safra kesesi duvar kalınlığı 0,43±0,21 cm'dir. Operasyonlar 10 farklı cerrah tarafından gerçekleştirilmiştir. Hastaların yaşının, safra kesesinde taş tespit edilme durumunun, tespit edilen taşın boyutunun ve preoperatif tetkiklerindeki WBC, CRP, D.Bilirubin ve KCFT değerlerinin yüksek olmasının piyesin bütünlüğü açısından belirleyici olmadığı sonucuna ulaşılmıştır. Hastaların cinsiyetinin, laparoskopik kolesistektomilerde endo-bag kullanımının, safra kesesi duvar kalınlığının ve operasyonu yapan cerrahın piyesin bütünlüğü açısından belirleyici olduğu sonucuna ulaşılmıştır. Sonuç: Laparoskopik kolesistektomide piyesin bütünlüğüne hastanın cinsiyeti, endo-bag kullanımı, safra kesesi duvar kalınlığı ve operasyonu yapan cerrah faktörleri açısından daha çok özen gösterilmelidir. İlave faktörler de dikkate alınarak laparoskopik kolesistektomide piyesin bütünlüğünü belirleyen faktörler retrospektif ve prospektif araştırmalarla daha sık incelenmelidir.

makaleler.baslik: Endoscopic versus microscopic ear surgery in surgical education: a systematic review.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Kulak Cerrahisi Eğitiminde Endoskopik ve Mikroskopik Yöntemlerin Karşılaştırılması
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 287 katılımcıyı içeren 8 çalışmanın meta-analizinde, endoskopik cerrahinin anatomik oryantasyon ve eğitim değerinde üstün olduğu, mikroskopik cerrahinin ise ileri teknik beceri kazanımında kritik kaldığı gösterilmiştir. Eğitimde her iki yöntemin entegrasyonu önerilmektedir.
makaleler.ozet:
OBJECTIVE: To systematically review the educational value of endoscopic ear surgery (EES) compared to microscopic ear surgery (MES) in otolaryngology training programs.
DATA SOURCES: PubMed, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, and Scopus (up to October 2025).
REVIEW METHODS: A systematic review was conducted following PRISMA guidelines. Studies comparing EES and MES in educational settings (cadaveric, live surgery, or simulation) involving medical students, residents, or fellows were included. Outcomes were categorized into cognitive (anatomical knowledge), psychomotor (technical skills), and affective (perceived educational value) domains. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2, ROBINS-I, and JBI tools, and the certainty of evidence was evaluated using the GRADE approach.
RESULTS: Eight studies (n = 287 participants) met the inclusion criteria. In the affective domain, EES was consistently rated higher for perceived educational value, optical quality, and anatomical visualization, particularly by junior trainees. In the cognitive domain, objective assessments of anatomical knowledge acquisition showed no significant difference between modalities, though EES provided a shared perspective beneficial for early orientation. In the psychomotor domain, MES was frequently preferred by senior trainees for developing bimanual dexterity and depth perception. The overall certainty of evidence was low to moderate due to study heterogeneity and reliance on subjective measures.
CONCLUSION: EES and MES offer complementary educational benefits. EES excels in early-phase anatomical orientation and shared visualization, while MES remains crucial for advanced technical skill refinement. Otolaryngology curricula should integrate both modalities sequentially to optimize surgical competency.

makaleler.baslik: Assessment of Interprofessional Trauma Team Performance and Cohesion During a Civil-Military Large-Scale Live Simulation Exercise-A Cross-Sectional Study.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Sivil-Askeri Travma Simülasyonunda Ekip Performansı ve Uyum Analizi
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 75 travma ekibinin katıldığı simülasyonda, ekiplerin kendi performanslarını değerlendirme puanları, uzman gözlemcilerden anlamlı derecede yüksek bulunmuştur (%57'ye karşı %25 mükemmel). Liderlik netliği ve yapılandırılmış iletişimin performansı artırdığı saptanmıştır.
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Large-scale civil-military simulation exercises allow interprofessional trauma teams practice leadership, communication, and decision-making under high stress; however, evidence on their contribution to multinational interoperability is limited. We assessed trauma-team performance and cohesion during a multinational live simulation and identified barriers and enablers of interoperability.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This prospective cross-sectional observational study was conducted during NATO Vigorous Warrior 2024 across eight Role 2 hospitals in Hungary. Trauma teams (n = 75) from nine nations managed simulated major trauma casualties. Performance was evaluated using the Non-Technical Skills for Surgeons (NOTSS) and Team Emergency Assessment Measure (TEAM) frameworks. Four expert assessors made structured observations, and members completed post-scenario self-assessments; team and assessor ratings were compared descriptively.
RESULTS: Teams rated their overall performance more favorably than assessors across all domains: overall performance was rated excellent by 57% of members versus 25% of assessors, who rated 25% of teams poor or below average. Discrepancies were greatest for leadership clarity, structured communication, and role allocation. Designated leadership, clear chains of command, and organized equipment were associated with better decision-making and task completion. Multinational composition enriched problem-solving but created communication barriers, tensions, and documentation inconsistencies; absent standardized debriefing further limited structured learning.
CONCLUSIONS: Leadership clarity, structured communication, and psychological safety underpin effective multinational trauma teamwork. The perceived-observed performance gap, which may reflect self-assessment leniency and assessor stringency ("hawk-dove" effect), indicates scope for calibration through structured feedback. Standardized training frameworks, harmonized resuscitation protocols, and structured debriefing are needed to improve interoperability and readiness across civil-military trauma systems.

makaleler.baslik: Assessing the Impact of Robotic Surgery on General Surgical Resident Training.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Genel Cerrahi Asistan Eğitiminde Robotik Cerrahinin Etkisi
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 2015-2021 arası 1436 robotik ve 5504 laparoskopik ameliyatın incelendiği çalışmada robotik cerrahi yaklaşık 6 kat arttı. Mevcut asistanların %59,1'i robotik cerrahinin laparoskopik beceri gelişimini engellediğini bildirdi.
makaleler.ozet:
OBJECTIVE: The prevalence of robotic surgery has grown exponentially since its U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approval in 2000. This shift in technology has raised questions about the impact on surgery resident training. There is concern that increased utilization of robotic surgery may result in deficiency in laparoscopic training. The aim of this study was to assess the recent impact of robotic surgery on general surgery resident training.
DESIGN: We performed a 2-phase study consisting of a retrospective review of institutional operative volume and a cross-sectional survey of current residents and alumni. A retrospective review of operative cases using the electronic medical record from 2015 to 2021 was performed to assess trends in common core minimally invasive surgical procedures. Following this, a quantitative, anonymous survey was sent to former and current general surgery residents who graduated after 2015.
SETTING: A mid-sized, university-affiliated academic general surgery residency program with 6 to 8 categorical residents per year.
PARTICIPANTS: Operative case data from all minimally invasive general surgery procedures performed at the institution between 2015 and 2021 were analyzed. An anonymous electronic survey was distributed to general surgery alumni (graduation years 2015-2022) and current residents (clinical years 2023-2028 cohort). A total of 75 residents were invited to participate.
RESULTS: From 2015 to 2021, 1436 robotic and 5504 laparoscopic surgeries were performed. There was a nearly 6-fold increase in robotic surgery over the study period. By 2021, both robotic ventral hernia repair and inguinal hernia repair volumes exceeded laparoscopic equivalents. Survey response rates were completed by 28/33 (85%) former alumni and 23/42 (55%) current residents. Majority of alumni (89.3%) reported good or excellent laparoscopic training experience compared with 39.1% of current residents. Most alumni and current residents reported good or excellent robotic training experience (67.9% and 82.6%, respectively). While nearly all alumni felt robotic surgery did not negatively impact laparoscopic training, 59.1% of current residents reported that robotic surgery has impeded their laparoscopic skill development.
CONCLUSIONS: Robotic surgery is increasing exponentially while laparoscopic surgical procedures have begun to decline. Residents may continue to perceive their laparoscopic experience as less robust than their robotic experience. Given the prolonged learning curve in laparoscopic surgery, it may be necessary to establish specific, defined minimum case requirements for laparoscopic surgery that are independent of robotic surgery.

makaleler.baslik: The competency trap: how work hour restrictions and low operative volume may produce persistent suboptimal proficiency in surgeons - a comparative analysis of Italy, Germany, The United States, and The United Kingdom.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Cerrahide Çalışma Saati Sınırlamaları ve Yetersizlik Tuzağı
makaleler.kisa_ozet: Çalışma saatleri kısıtlamaları ve düşük vaka hacimlerinin karmaşık prosedürlerde kalıcı yetersizlik riski ("kompetans tuzağı") oluşturabileceği teorik bir sentezle incelendi. İtalya, Almanya, ABD ve İngiltere eğitim gereksinimleri karşılaştırıldı.
makaleler.ozet: Work hour restrictions for surgical trainees reduce fatigue-related errors but may inadvertently limit operative volume. This paper introduces the concept of a "competency trap": a theoretical risk, supported by indirect evidence, whereby the interaction between work hour limits and low case volume may produce a surgeon who is well-rested but at risk of persistent suboptimal proficiency for complex procedures. We conducted a conceptual synthesis of literature on surgical learning curves, skill decay, volume-outcome relationships, and work hour regulations. We analyzed training requirements in Italy (DM 68/2015), Germany (Arbeitszeitgesetz, Logbuch), the United States (ACGME), and the United Kingdom (NHS, ePortfolio). Illustrative volume data from the Piemonte region (PNE 2022) are presented as a lower-bound case study. A mathematical model with sensitivity analysis was constructed across multiple procedure types. Learning curves vary by procedure: short (C = 60, cholecystectomy), medium (C = 75, colectomy), long (C = 90, bariatric surgery), very long tier 1 (C = 100, pancreatectomy, hepatectomy), and very long tier 2 (C = 120, esophagectomy). Italy faces structural vulnerabilities: low first-operator percentage (10% for high-complexity cases, effectively 3 independent cases), no mandatory electronic logbook, and ongoing EU infringement proceedings for work hour non-enforcement. Germany permits Opt-Out to 58-hour weeks with eLogbuch transparency. The United States mandates 850 major cases (200 as chief resident) with electronic verification. The United Kingdom has fully enforced 48-hour EWTD limits without opt-out and a mandatory ePortfolio, but has lost over 3 million training opportunities since 2020 (organizational estimate). Using Piemonte as a lower-bound case study (V_p = 5 cases/year), the trap is present across all procedures. Under optimistic assumptions (K₀=20, V_p = 12), the trap resolves for colectomy (V_m = 10) but persists for bariatric surgery (V_m = 12.5). Under lower-bound volume assumptions derived from the Piemonte case study, Italy and the United Kingdom face theoretical competency trap risk across a wide range of procedures. Solutions require reformed minimums with higher first-operator percentages, mandatory electronic logbooks, hub-and-spoke centralization, simulation-based maintenance, and resolution of work hour implementation gaps with adequate staffing.

makaleler.baslik: Evaluating the Quality and Accessibility of Integrated Vascular Surgery Residency Program Websites for Prospective Applicants.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Vasküler Cerrahi Asistanlık Programı Web Sitelerinin Kalite ve Erişilebilirlik Değerlendirmesi
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 81 vasküler cerrahi programının incelendiği çalışmada, web sitelerinin %98,8'inin aktif olduğu ancak program direktörü iletişim bilgilerinin sadece %40,7'sinde, operatif hacim verilerinin ise sadece %12,3'ünde erişilebilir olduğu saptanmıştır.
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: The COVID-19 pandemic prompted a shift to virtual residency interviews, although approximately half of integrated vascular surgery residency (VSR) programs have since returned to an in-person format. Amidst this evolving landscape, program websites have remained an invaluable resource for candidates to learn about VSR programs. In this study, we examined whether VSR program websites provide adequate and current information for residency candidates.
METHODS: A list of all active VSR programs was obtained from the Association of American Medical Colleges (AAMC) Electronic Residency Application Service (ERAS) website. Each program's website was reviewed in November 2025, and data were collected regarding program structure, faculty and current resident rosters, application requirements, and publicly available formal policies.
RESULTS: Of the 81 active programs, 80 (98.8%) had a formal residency program website. Information on residency program structure was reported in the majority of websites, including mission statement (91.4%), rotation and curriculum data (65.4%), rotating sites (61.7%), educational conferences (64.2%), and resident research experience (56.8%). Only ten programs (12.3%) reported resident operative volumes. Information regarding the residency program director (PD; 91.4%), program coordinator (PC; 92.6%), teaching faculty (92.6%), and current residents (81.5%) was available in most websites. However, with the exception of the PC (91.4%), contact information for the PD (40.7%), faculty (29.6%), and residents (13.6%) was not easily accessible. The majority of websites had a "how to apply" section (86.4%), but relatively few reported their interview dates (30.9%). Resident experience videos were available in less than half of websites (39.5%). Data on salary (53.1%), resident benefits (53.1%), vacation policies (27.2%), and academic conference policies (28.4%) were also inconsistently reported.
CONCLUSIONS: Residency program websites remain a central resource for applicants, particularly in the current era of virtual and hybrid interview formats. In this study, we found substantial variability in the information presented across VSR program websites, with a notable lack of accessible contact information for program leadership, faculty, and residents. Enhancing website content and transparency may better support applicants as they evaluate programs and prepare for the residency application process.

makaleler.baslik: Self-supervised learning for determining the presence and site of bowel obstruction on upright abdominal radiography.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Batın Grafisinde Bağırsak Tıkanıklığı için Yarı Gözetimli Öğrenme
makaleler.kisa_ozet: Toplam 1500 etiketli ve 1922 etiketlenmemiş grafinin kullanıldığı çalışmada, önerilen SSL modelleri üstün sınıflandırma performansı göstermiştir (VGG16 tabanlı doğruluk 0,846; ResNet50 tabanlı 0,833). Bu modeller, denetimli modellere ve kıdemli bir radyoloğa kıyasla istatistiksel olarak anlamlı üstünlük sergilemiştir (p<0,05).
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Detecting and localizing bowel obstruction on upright abdominal radiograph is a challenging task, and ground truth typically relies on imaging examinations, endoscopy or surgical notes within a short time window. The lack of ground truth leads to poor performance on supervised learning. To address this issue, self-supervised learning (SSL) is used to determine the presence and site of bowel obstruction using few labeled samples.
METHODS: A total of 1500 labeled and 1922 unlabeled radiographs were categorized based on the ground truth. The SSL model was firstly trained on the unlabeled radiographs, and then fine-tuned on the labeled radiographs. ResNet50 and VGG16 were used for the embedded base encoders, whose weights and parameters were adjusted during training process. Furthermore, it was tested on an external dataset, compared with supervised learning models and human interpreters. Finally, the t-SNE and Grad-CAM were used to visualize the model's interpretation.
RESULTS: The proposed SSL models showed superior classification performance (VGG16-backboned: accuracy of 0.846, MCC of 0.873, Kappa of 0.770; ResNet50-backboned: 0.833, 0.860, 0.750), outperformed supervised models (Mean: 0.750, 0.792, 0.625) and a senior radiologist (0.748, 0.791, 0.620). Significant statistical differences were observed between VGG16-backboned SSL model and supervised models, as well as human interpreters (P < 0.05). Additionally, the SSL model exhibited better cluster performance through t-SNE and demonstrated outstanding lesion recognition ability through Grad-CAM.
CONCLUSIONS: The proposed SSL model exhibited outstanding performance in determining the presence and site of bowel obstruction on upright abdominal radiography based on unlabeled images and limited ground truth, indicating the potential of SSL for computer-aided diagnosis of diseases that are difficult and time-consuming for labeling.

makaleler.baslik: Impact of AI-assisted Sedation on Early Cognitive Function and Sleep Quality in the Elderly Undergoing GI Endoscopy.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Yaşlılarda Endoskopi Sonrası Yapay Zekâ Destekli Sedasyonun Etkileri
makaleler.kisa_ozet: GİS endoskopi yapılacak 180 yaşlı hastayla yürütülen RCT'de, yapay zekâ destekli sedasyon grubunda derlenme süresi ve yönsel güç toparlanması anlamlı düzeyde daha kısa bulunmuştur. Yapay zekâ destekli sedasyon erken bilişsel işlevi etkilemezken, prosedür gecesinde uyku kalitesini artırmıştır.
makaleler.ozet:
OBJECTIVE: This study investigated the effect of ENDOANGLE-assisted sedation by the "ENDOANGLE" on early cognitive function and sleep quality in elderly patients after gastrointestinal endoscopy.
METHODS: A total of 180 patients (aged 65-80, American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) I-III) scheduled for sedated endoscopy were randomly assigned to an ENDOANGLE-assisted group (AI group, n = 87) or a control group (C group, n = 85). We recorded procedural metrics (induction time, resuscitation time, directional force recovery, propofol dose), Ramsay scores, vital signs, and adverse events. Sleep quality was evaluated using the St. Mary's Hospital Sleep Questionnaire (SMH score) and actigraphy (Honor Band 6) at baseline (T0), on bowel preparation day (T1), post-procedure evening (T2), and 3 (T3) and 7 (T4) days post-procedure. Cognitive function was assessed with the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE), Verbal Fluency Test (VFT), Clock Drawing Test (CDT), and Trail Making Tests A and B (TMT-A/B) before examination (T1), 30 minutes post-emergence (T2), and at 3 (T3) and 7 (T4) days postprocedure.
RESULTS: The resuscitation time and directional force recovery in the AI group were significantly shorter than those in the C group. The induction time and total amount of propofol administered during examinations were comparable between the two groups. There were no statistically significant differences in cognitive test scores across time points between the two groups; however, on the day of enema administration, SMH scores in both groups were significantly lower than baseline. However, at night, the AI group had significantly higher SMH scores compared to the C group. On the third and seventh days after surgery, there were no differences in SMH scores from baseline within each group or between the two groups, and the sleep monitoring results from the Honor Band were largely consistent with the SMH scoring system.
DISCUSSION: AI-assisted sedation with ENDOANGEL improved sleep quality on the procedure night in elderly patients but did not affect cognitive function or sleep at 3 and 7 days postoperatively. This early benefit may stem from optimized propofol titration, which reduces acute sleep disruption. The transient effect and unchanged cognition underscore the safety and limited duration of AI impact. Future research should explore mechanisms and whether early sleep improvement enhances overall recovery.
CONCLUSION: AI-assisted sedation showed no difference in early cognitive function compared to conventional sedation, despite both groups experiencing transient post-procedural cognitive changes. The ENDOANGEL system can improve sleep quality in elderly patients at night. However, it did not affect sleep quality on the third and seventh days after painless gastrointestinal endoscopy.

makaleler.baslik: Deep Learning for Real-Time Image Interpretation in Arthroscopy: A Systematic Review of Classification, Segmentation, and Detection Tasks.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Artroskopide Gerçek Zamanlı Görüntü Yorumlama İçin Derin Öğrenme
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 6 heterojen çalışmanın incelendiği sistematik derlemede, derin öğrenmenin enstrüman tanımada yüksek doğruluk (%99,1'e varan, duyarlılık=0,988) ve kanama çerçevesi tespiti (%95,8, duyarlılık=97,3) sağladığı gösterilmiştir. Segmentasyon en güçlü sonucu büyük kemik yapılarında verirken, hiçbir çalışmada cerrahi karar veya hasta sonuçlarına etkisi değerlendirilmemiştir.
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Deep learning (DL) is increasingly applied to arthroscopic video for instrument recognition, anatomical segmentation, and intraoperative event detection. The performance, architectures, and real-time feasibility of these systems remain incompletely characterized. This systematic review aimed to evaluate the performance, architectures, and real-time feasibility of DL for classification, segmentation, and detection in arthroscopic video interpretation.
METHODS: Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020, PubMed/ MEDLINE, Ovid, and the Cochrane Library were searched (February 2025), supplemented by artificial intelligence-assisted queries (Elicit, Undermind). Eligible studies applied DL to arthroscopy for classification, segmentation, or detection with quantitative performance and/or inference speed. Two reviewers independently screened, extracted, and assessed quality using Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies-2; the protocol was registered in International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews.
RESULTS: Six studies met inclusion criteria (knee = 2, shoulder = 2, wrist = 1, non-site-specific bleeding = 1). Classification achieved high accuracy for instrument recognition (up to 99.1%, sensitivity = 0.988) and bleeding- frame detection (95.8%, sensitivity = 97.3%). Segmentation was strongest for large bony structures (Dice 0.79-0.89) and weakest for deformable tissues (meniscus Dice = 0.48). U-Net variants (U-Net++, DeepLab v3+) predominated with frequent transfer learning. Two studies achieved real-time inference (15-60 frames per second). Risk of bias was high across all studies.
CONCLUSION: Based on 6 heterogeneous studies, DL appears technically feasible for arthroscopic image interpretation, particularly instrument classification and osseous segmentation, though findings should be interpreted as preliminary. No study evaluated impact on surgical decision-making or patient outcomes, and none was deployed prospectively in live surgery. Translation will require multicentre datasets, standardized reporting, and prospective evaluation against clinically meaningful endpoints. Cite this article as: Lasslett C, Reddy R, Giritharan G, et al. Deep learning for real-time image interpretation in arthroscopy: a systematic review of classification, segmentation, and detection tasks. Eurasian J Med. 2026, 58(4), 1415, doi: 10.5152/ eurasianjmed.2026.261415.

makaleler.baslik: Chinese expert consensus on AI-assisted clinical decision-making in organ transplantation.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Organ Naklinde Yapay Zekâ Destekli Klinik Karar Uzman Konsensusu
makaleler.kisa_ozet: Çin'deki organ bağışı ve nakli süreçlerinde yapay zekânın standardizasyonunu sağlamak amacıyla çok disiplinli uzmanlar tarafından bir konsensus oluşturulmuştur. Bu uzlaşı, donör değerlendirmesinden post-transplant yönetime kadar tüm klinik senaryoları kapsayan teknik bir çerçeve sunmaktadır.
makaleler.ozet: Organ donation and transplantation in China have developed rapidly, ranking second in the world in terms of both donation and transplantation volume. However, both the quantity and quality of organ transplants remain to be further improved to satisfy the demands of the vast number of patients awaiting transplantation. Artificial intelligence (AI) facilitates the integration, analysis, and application of multisource clinical big data. It is capable of assisting in expanding the pool of available donor organs and enhancing graft quality, thereby providing a novel technological foundation for alleviating the imbalance between the supply and demand of transplant organs. To standardize the auxiliary application of AI throughout the entire process of organ donation and transplantation in China, we convened a team of multidisciplinary experts to formulate the Chinese Expert Consensus on AI-Assisted Clinical Decision-Making in Organ Transplantation. By establishing unified requirements for data and models, this consensus forms a technical framework covering clinical scenarios across the entire workflow of organ donation and transplantation, including donor assessment and maintenance, organ matching, organ preservation and transportation, transplant surgery, and post-transplant recipient management. Furthermore, it clarifies ethical and regulatory constraints as well as the boundaries of responsibility subjects. This work aimed to further enhance the standardization and safety of AI-assisted organ donation and transplantation, ultimately promoting the high-quality development of this field in China.

makaleler.baslik: The evolving landscape of artificial intelligence in cholecystectomy: a bibliometric and science-mapping analysis.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Kolesistektomide Yapay Zekanın Evrilen Görünümü
makaleler.kisa_ozet: Kolesistektomide yapay zeka araştırmalarının küresel dağılımını inceleyen bibliyometrik analizde 559 yayın değerlendirildi. Yayınların %75,8'i 2022-2025 yılları arasında yayımlandı ve çalışmalar iş akışı analizi ile bilgisayarla görme odaklı uygulamalara kaydı.
makaleler.ozet: To map the global research landscape and thematic evolution of artificial intelligence (AI)-related research in cholecystectomy and to identify major contributors, collaboration patterns, and intellectual foundations. English-language articles and reviews were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection and Scopus. After deduplication and eligibility screening, 559 publications were included. Publication trends, scientific collaboration, keyword co-occurrence, conceptual structure, thematic evolution, and co-citation and citation-burst patterns were analyzed using bibliometrix, VOSviewer, and Python. Research activity increased markedly in recent years, with 424 publications (75.8%) appearing between 2022 and 2025. China contributed the largest publication output, whereas the United States received the highest total citations. Keyword and conceptual-structure analyses identified research domains involving AI and computational methods, surgical workflow and intraoperative visual analysis, and computer-vision-based applications. Thematic evolution suggested a progression from early workflow- and convolutional-neural-network-related research toward machine learning, deep learning, radiomics, surgical phase recognition, and more recent transformer-related approaches. Twinanda et al. [1] showed the strongest citation burst and occupied a prominent position in the reference co-citation network. AI-related research in cholecystectomy has expanded rapidly and become increasingly diverse in its methodological and application-oriented focus. Current bibliometric patterns suggest growing attention to workflow analysis, computer vision, surgical phase recognition, and newer model architectures. Further multicenter validation and prospective clinical evaluation are needed to determine whether these developments translate into generalizable and clinically meaningful applications.

makaleler.baslik: Complex and Simple Appendicitis: REstrictive or Liberal Postoperative Antibiotic eXposure (CASA RELAX) Using Desirability of Outcome Ranking and Response Adjusted for Duration of Antibiotic Risk: A Multicenter Bayesian Randomized Controlled Trial.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Akut Apandisitte Restriktif Postoperatif Antibiyotik Tedavisi
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 346 hastanın dahil olduğu çok merkezli Bayesian RCT'de, akut apandisitte restriktif postoperatif antibiyotik stratejisi, liberal stratejiye kıyasla benzer ila hafif düzeyde iyileşmiş klinik sonuçlar gösterdi (kümülatif OR 0,84; %95 CrI 0,42-1,72). Restriktif stratejiden en çok fayda görenler komplike apandisiti olan hastalardı (OR 0,69).
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: The optimal duration of antibiotic agents after appendectomy for simple or complicated (gangrenous or perforated) appendicitis is unknown. We performed a randomized trial to compare a Restrictive to a Liberal post-operative antibiotic strategy, after appendectomy.
METHODS: Adults undergoing appendectomy were randomized 1:1 to a Restrictive (no post-operative antibiotic agents for simple, up to 1 d for complicated) or Liberal (up to 1 d for simple, 4 d for complicated) strategy. The primary endpoint was on the basis of Desirability of Outcome Ranking (DOOR)/Response Adjusted for Duration of Antibiotic Risk (RADAR), an ordinal scale of mutually exclusive clinical complications with within-category rankings determined by duration of antibiotic exposure. Bayesian cumulative logistic models using a neutral prior were used to assess the Posterior probability (PP) of benefit with a Restrictive strategy. Type of appendicitis (simple vs. complicated) was assessed as an interaction.
RESULTS: A total of 346 subjects enrolled from 9 sites were included in the final analysis. Baseline demographics between groups were similar. There were 265 simple and 81 complicated (11 gangrenous) appendicitis cases. The Restrictive strategy, had a cumulative odds ratio of 0.84 (95% credible interval [CrI] 0.42-1.72), a 68% PP that Restrictive tactic reduces (improves) the DOOR category. This was driven by patients with complicated appendicitis with an OR 0.69 (95% CrI: 0.27-1.68), a 79% probability that the Restrictive strategy, reduces DOOR. In the RADAR analysis, the Restrictive strategy, had an 80% PP of a more desirable overall outcome compared with the Liberal strategy.
CONCLUSIONS: A restrictive post-operative antibiotic strategy, in acute appendicitis resulted in similar to mildly improved clinical outcomes, when compared with a Liberal strategy. The patients who benefitted most from a Restrictive strategy, were patients with complicated appendicitis.

makaleler.baslik: PROphylactic use of closed incision negative Pressure wound thERapy for VASCular surgery groin incisions: recommendations from an international expert-based consensus (PROPER-VASC).
makaleler.baslik_tr: Vasküler Cerrahi Kasık Kesilerinde Negatif Basınçlı Yara Tedavisi
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 20 uzmanın katıldığı Delphi konsensus çalışmasında, vasküler cerrahide kasık kesileri sonrası profilaktik kapalı insizyon negatif basınçlı yara tedavisinin (ciNPWT) yüzeysel cerrahi alan enfeksiyonlarını azaltma potansiyeli konusunda uzlaşıya varıldı. Yüksek riskli hastalarda rutin, standart riskli hastalarda ise bireyselleştirilmiş olarak kullanılması önerildi.
makaleler.ozet:
OBJECTIVE: This study aims to obtain experts' consensus and define recommendations regarding best clinical practices on the use of prophylactic close incision negative wound pressure therapy (ciNPWT) in patients undergoing groin incisions in vascular surgery METHODS: A modified Delphi consensus methodology was employed over three rounds, involving a panel of 20 experts, by using a four point likert scale. Statements that reached consensus at the first round were submitted to a second round, unmodified. Statements that failed the first round were adapted and proposed to the second and third rounds of judgment. Agreement and consistency derived from the three rounds were used to develop recommendations on the prophylactic use of ciNPWT on groin incisions after vascular operations.
RESULTS: After three rounds, 3 statements were rejected, and 20 recommendations were made. Six received a Grade B consensus, and fourteen statements reached a Grade A consensus. Experts agree on the potential of ciNPWT in reducing superficial groin SSI in patients with high-risk features, which should consequently be treated with such technology routinely, contrary to standard-risk patients who would not benefit as much from ciNPWT dressings. Practical recommendations that reached consensus included the use of ciNPWT as soon as possible after surgery, possibly already in the operating theater, and devices should stay in place for 5-7 days.
CONCLUSIONS: Inguinal ciNPWT should be used in patients at increased risk of SSI and wound dehiscence after vascular interventions to prevent superficial infections. Individualized risk assessment should be performed for each patient to guide decision-making and practical instructions for device management should be provided.

makaleler.baslik: Risk factors for postoperative infection in patients with oral cancer: a meta-analysis.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Oral Kanser Hastalarında Postoperatif Enfeksiyon Risk Faktörleri
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 5334 oral kanser hastasının incelendiği meta-analizde, diyabet ve uzamış operasyon süresinin cerrahi alan enfeksiyonu (SSI) ile anlamlı düzeyde ilişkili olduğu tespit edildi. Mandibulektomi ve perioperatif kan transfüzyonu ise yüksek etki büyüklüğü gösterse de istatistiksel olarak anlamlı düzeye ulaşmadı.
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Surgical site infection (SSI) is a frequent complication after oral cancer surgery, adversely affecting patient outcomes. Given the inconsistencies in previous studies, this meta-analysis aimed to identify reliable risk factors to inform strategies for SSI prevention and to improve postoperative care.
METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted using four databases (PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science) up to January 2024 to identify SSI risk factors in head and neck cancer. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias. Analysis was performed using Stata 15.1.
RESULTS: Thirteen studies involving 5334 oral cancer patients identified diabetes and prolonged operative time as significant factors associated with SSI, while mandibulectomy and perioperative blood transfusion showed elevated effect sizes but did not reach statistical significance in the pooled multivariate analysis. Additional potential factors included male gender, smoking, tracheostomy, and neck dissection. Findings were consistent across studies.
CONCLUSION: Diabetes and prolonged operative time were significantly associated with increased risk of SSI, whereas mandibulectomy and perioperative blood transfusion showed possible clinical relevance but remained statistically uncertain. Early identification and targeted management of high-risk individuals may help reduce infection rates and improve outcomes.

makaleler.baslik: Antibiotic Prophylaxis in Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery: A Systematic Literature Review.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Metabolik ve Bariatrik Cerrahide Antibiyotik Profilaksisi
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 8 çalışmanın incelendiği sistematik derlemede, mevcut kanıtların tüm metabolik ve bariatrik cerrahi prosedürlerinde rutin antibiyotik profilaksisini (AP) desteklemediği bildirildi. Temiz cerrahi alanlarda (örneğin SG) rutin AP gereksiz olabilirken, kontamine riski olanlarda yüksek riskli hastalar için seçici kullanım gerekebilir.
makaleler.ozet:
INTRODUCTION: Metabolic and bariatric surgery (MBS) is the most effective treatment for obesity, yet obesity increases the risk of perioperative complications, including surgical site infections (SSIs). Although MBS are classified as clean or clean-contaminated, current guidelines recommend antibiotic prophylaxis (AP) for all such operations, despite the lack of clear clinical evidence supporting this approach.
AIM: To assess the effect of AP on the incidence of surgical site infection (SSI) rate and other postoperative outcomes after metabolic and bariatric procedures.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A systematic search used the terms "Bariatric Surgery" and "Antibiotic Prophylaxis," with added queries for SG, RYGB, OAGB, SADI, SASI, and AGB. Eligible designs included randomized trials and observational studies that reported clinical outcomes such as SSI, wound complications, morbidity, or mortality. Reports without original clinical data were excluded. Data were analyzed separately for clean procedures (SG, AGB) and clean-contaminated procedures (RYGB, SADI, SASI).
RESULTS: Eight studies met criteria. Only three studies directly compared AP with no prophylaxis in clean and clean- -contaminated operations and found no significant reduction in SSI rates. In clean procedures, available evidence consistently does not support routine antibiotic use. In clean-contaminated procedures, the available results were underpowered. Isolated studies suggested a modest benefit in selected subgroups, yet none reached statistical significance. Vancomycin may be associated with increased infection risk. Ertapenem was associated with lower infection rates compared with ceftriaxone in open gastric bypass. Single retrospective studies linked lowered postoperative weight loss with levofloxacin use and clindamycin with a higher rate of hypertension remission, but this evidence is weak.
DISCUSSION: Current evidence does not provide strong support for routine perioperative AP in all MBS procedures. Current evidence suggests that routine AP may be unnecessary in selected clean procedures such as SG. In clean-contaminated procedures, selective use may be justified for high-risk patients, but additional studies are required to identify this group. When used, prophylaxis should be weight-adjusted, timed appropriately, and repeated intraoperatively when indicated.
CONCLUSIONS: Currently available evidence does not support the routine use of AP in all MBS procedures for reducing SSI rates. Especially in clean field procedures this prophylaxis might not be justified. In clean-contaminated procedures, selective use may be justified for high-risk patients. The current level of evidence is rather weak and further studies are needed to evaluate both infectious and metabolic endpoints to develop evidence-based AP strategies in metabolic and bariatric surgery.

makaleler.baslik: Prospective comparative evaluation of povidone-iodine sitz bath and silver-based antimicrobial spray in postoperative perianal wound care: impact on healing outcomes, patient satisfaction, and treatment compliance.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Perianal Yara Bakımında Povidon-İyot ve Gümüş Sprey Karşılaştırması
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 100 hastalık gözlemsel çalışmada, povidon-iyot sitz banyosu gümüş bazlı spreye kıyasla daha kısa yara iyileşme süresi (14,2 güne karşı 16,8 gün; p=0,001) ve daha düşük SSI oranı (%6'ya karşı %18; p=0,048) sağladı. Gümüş sprey ise daha düşük postoperatif ağrı ve daha yüksek hasta memnuniyeti ile ilişkilendirildi.
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Perianal surgical wounds are likely to take longer to heal and get infected due to constant contamination, moisture and pain during defecation. Povidone-iodine has long been applied in the postoperative treatment, and silver-based agents have become an alternative with an excellent antimicrobial effect and patient-friendly characteristics.
AIM: This study was intended to compare the outcomes on postoperative perianal wound-healing between the application of povidone-iodine sitz bath and silver-based antimicrobial spray, with additional evaluation of patient satisfaction and treatment compliance with the assigned wound care regimen.
METHODS: It is a hospital-based observational study conducted over a period of 4 months in a tertiary care centre. A total of one hundred patients subjected to surgery for haemorrhoids, fissure in ano, or fistula in ano were recruited and split into two equal groups. Group A received a povidone-iodine sitz bath, and Group B received a silver-based antimicrobial spray. The main outcome was time to heal wounds. The secondary outcomes were postoperative pain (VAS), patient satisfaction score (PSS), treatment compliance index (TCI), and wound-related complications. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05.
RESULTS: Baseline characteristics were comparable among groups. Mean wound-healing time was significantly shorter in the povidone-iodine cohort (14.2 ± 3.1 days) compared to the silver group (16.8 ± 3.6 days; p = 0.001). Surgical site infection was lower with povidone-iodine (6% vs. 18%; p = 0.048). Silver-based spray was associated with significantly lower postoperative pain scores, higher patient satisfaction scores (composite PSS: 7.9 ± 0.9 vs. 6.5 ± 1.1; p < 0.001), and superior treatment compliance at both Week 2 (92.1% vs. 74.2%; p < 0.001) and Week 4 (88.4% vs. 66.8%; p < 0.001). Wound-related complications were more frequent in the silver cohort.
CONCLUSION: Povidone-iodine sitz bath provides superior healing and infection control, whereas silver-based antimicrobial spray significantly improves postoperative comfort, patient satisfaction, and treatment compliance highlighting the importance of patient-centred factors in wound care selection following perianal surgery.

gundem.baslik: Oral versus intravenous postoperative antibiotics after laparoscopic appendectomy following complicated appendicitis: an open-label cluster-randomized cluster-crossover multiperiod non-inferiority study.
gundem.baslik_tr: Komplike Apandisit Sonrası Oral ve İntravenöz Antibiyotik Karşılaştırması
gundem.kisa_ozet: 12 Danimarka hastanesinde komplike apandisit nedeniyle laparoskopik apendektomi yapılan 1021 hastada, 3 günlük oral ve intravenöz antibiyotik rejimleri karşılaştırıldı. İntra-abdominal abse insidansı oral grupta %6,8, intravenöz grupta %4,9 olarak saptandı ve oral tedavinin non-inferior olduğu gösterildi. Oral antibiyotikler hastane kalış süresini kısalttı (-41,1 saat), ancak yeniden yatış oranını artırdı (fark %4,7).
gundem.ozet:
BACKGROUND: The optimal administration route and duration of postoperative antibiotics for complicated appendicitis after source control remain debated. The aim of this non-inferiority cluster-randomized trial was to compare oral versus intravenous antibiotics following laparoscopic appendectomy.
METHODS: In this pragmatic, open-label, cluster-randomized, cluster-crossover, non-inferiority trial across 12 Danish hospitals, adults undergoing laparoscopic appendectomy for complicated appendicitis received either a 3-day oral or intravenous postoperative antibiotic regimen. The primary outcome was 30-day intra-abdominal abscess, analysed in both intention-to-treat and per-protocol populations using a 5% points non-inferiority margin. Secondary 30-day outcomes included length of hospital stay, readmission, and postoperative complications.
RESULTS: Of 5424 patients screened, 1021 with complicated appendicitis were allocated to oral (n = 567) or intravenous (n = 454) antibiotics. In the intention-to-treat analysis, intra-abdominal abscess occurred in 39 of 567 oral and 22 of 454 intravenous patients; weighted 30-day incidences were 6.8% and 4.9% (absolute risk difference, 1.9%; 90% c.i., -0.4 to 4.2), meeting non-inferiority. In the per-protocol analysis, abscess occurred in 19 of 395 and 9 of 294 patients; weighted incidences were 4.9% and 3.0% (absolute risk difference, 1.8%; 90% c.i., -0.3 to 3.9). Oral antibiotics shortened hospital stay (-41.1 h; 95% c.i., -46.7 to -35.6) but increased readmission (difference, 4.7%; 95% c.i., 0.5 to 8.9).
CONCLUSIONS: A 3-day oral antibiotic regimen was non-inferior to intravenous antibiotic therapy in preventing intra-abdominal abscess after laparoscopic appendectomy for complicated appendicitis. Reduced hospital stay and comparable clinical outcomes support oral antibiotics as a routine postoperative option in clinically stable patients.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04803422.

gundem.baslik: Intraoperative core competencies in oncoplastic breast surgery: Recommendations from the international breastics Working Group.
gundem.baslik_tr: Onkoplastik Meme Cerrahisinde İntraoperatif Çekirdek Yeterlilikler Konsensus Önerileri
gundem.kisa_ozet: Uluslararası çalışma grubu, onkoplastik meme cerrahisinde teknik beceriler, doku yönetimi ve marjin değerlendirmesi dahil intraoperatif temel yeterlilikleri tanımlamıştır. Rehber, ameliyat sırasındaki hataları azaltmayı ve multidisipliner koordinasyonu güçlendirmeyi hedeflemektedir.
gundem.ozet: The intraoperative phase of oncoplastic breast surgery (OPBS) transforms multidisciplinary preoperative planning into technical execution that determines oncologic safety, reconstructive success and immediate postoperative outcomes. This manuscript - the Intraoperative Curriculum in a three-part competency series - defines core intraoperative knowledge, technical skills and non-technical behaviors required to perform OPBS safely and effectively. Domains addressed include team communication and structured briefings, confirmation of consent and operative plan, marking and localization verification, positioning and draping, oncologic excision and specimen orientation, tissue handling and perfusion preservation, oncoplastic reconstructive techniques (volume displacement and replacement), implant and flap management, intraoperative margin assessment tools, hemostasis and blood management, asepsis and device management, intraoperative documentation, debriefing, and escalation/referral pathways for complex cases. Each domain provides core competencies, rationale, competency level/type (basic/intermediate/advanced; knowledge/skill/attitude), suggested learning environments and practical sign-off recommendations. The curriculum supports consistent intraoperative practice, reduces preventable errors, facilitates multidisciplinary coordination (especially with radiation oncology and pathology) and prepares trainees for supervised autonomy in OPBS.

gundem.baslik: Transverse versus longitudinal mucosotomy during peroral endoscopic myotomy: results of a multicenter randomized controlled trial.
gundem.baslik_tr: POEM İşleminde Transvers ve Longitudinal Mukozotomi Karşılaştırması
gundem.kisa_ozet: 140 hastalık çok merkezli RCT'de, transvers mukozotomi submukozal tünele girişi hızlandırdı (228 sn'ye karşı 269 sn), hemostaz ihtiyacını azalttı (RR 0,68) ve pnömoperitoneum riskini düşürdü (RR 0,67). Yöntem, POEM prosedüründe verimliliği artırmaktadır.
gundem.ozet:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Peroral endoscopic myotomy (POEM) is an established first-line therapy for achalasia; however, technical variability persists in key procedural steps. The optimal orientation of mucosal entry remains uncertain. We evaluated whether transverse mucosotomy improves procedural efficiency and reduces gas-related events compared with the conventional longitudinal approach.
METHODS: In this multicenter, parallel-group randomized clinical trial conducted at three tertiary centers, 140 adults undergoing POEM were assigned (1:1) to a standardized 15-mm transverse or longitudinal mucosotomy. The primary outcome was time from initial mucosal incision to effective entry into the submucosal tunnel, assessed by independent anonymized video review using predefined objective timestamp criteria. Secondary outcomes included need for hemostasis, mucosotomy closure time, number of clips used, gas-related events, and 30-day complications. Analyses followed the intention-to-treat principle.
RESULTS: All randomized patients were included in the primary analysis. Transverse mucosotomy significantly reduced time to submucosal entry (median 228 vs. 269 s; adjusted mean difference - 44 s; 95% CI - 78 to - 10), need for hemostasis (38.6% vs. 57.1%; relative risk 0.68; 95% CI 0.49-0.95), closure time (662 vs. 1020 s; p < 0.001), and number of clips used (median 3 vs. 7; rate ratio 0.44; 95% CI 0.36-0.54). Pneumoperitoneum occurred less frequently with the transverse approach (34.3% vs. 51.4%; relative risk 0.67; 95% CI 0.46-0.97). Rates of serious adverse events and 30-day readmission were low and comparable between groups.
CONCLUSIONS: In a multicenter randomized trial, transverse mucosotomy during POEM improved intraoperative efficiency and reduced gas-related events without compromising short-term safety. These findings support mucosal entry orientation as a modifiable technical factor that may optimize procedural workflow and resource utilization in submucosal endoscopic surgery.

gundem.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Bariatric surgery effectively treats obesity and related co-morbidities, but the magnitude and durability of long-term mortality benefit compared with nonsurgical management remain poorly characterized.
OBJECTIVES: To synthesize the longest-term available mortality data comparing bariatric surgery with nonsurgical weight management in patients with obesity.
SETTING: Large-scale meta-analysis.
METHODS: A meta-analysis was conducted of studies published between 2000 and 2025 reporting mortality outcomes after sleeve gastrectomy or Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB) compared with control cohorts with obesity. Survival at all available postoperative intervals was evaluated. Mixed-effects meta-regression assessed patient-specific modifiers of mortality, whereas random-effects meta-analyses evaluated timepoint-specific mortality and cause-of-death differences.
RESULTS: Thirty-four studies including 449,957 patients were analyzed. Early postoperative mortality was low across all cohorts. Over a longer follow-up, bariatric surgery was associated with lower cumulative mortality compared with nonsurgical controls. At 7 years, pooled mortality was 2.64% in controls, 1.64% following RYGB, and .76% following sleeve gastrectomy. At 12 years, mortality remained lower after RYGB (4.34%) compared with controls (7.11%). Among patients with type 2 diabetes, mortality at 5 years was substantially lower following RYGB compared with diabetic controls (2.29% versus 11.0%). Cause-of-death analysis demonstrated fewer cancer-related deaths after RYGB (odds ratio, .46; 95% confidence interval, .31-.70) but higher proportions of deaths due to accidents, substance abuse, and suicide.
CONCLUSIONS: Bariatric surgery is associated with durable reductions in long-term mortality compared with nonsurgical management of obesity, particularly among patients with type 2 diabetes, supporting its role as an important intervention for improving long-term survival in severe obesity.
